newsitem.title: CHINA: China unveils rules to curb mining accidents.
newsitem.headline: China unveils rules to curb mining accidents.

text.p: China has issued regulations aimed at improving mining safety and stem a rising tide of mining accidents which claim 10,000 lives each year, the China Daily said on Wednesday.

It said the new rules, promulgated last week, would toughen enforcement of an existing mining safety law by outlining steps for handling mine accidents and by detailing legal culpability for those responsible for mining disasters.

"The regulation is a tool to urge local government(s) and mines to abide by the safety law to avoid the growing number of mining accidents," the newspaper quoted Liu Guangyi, director of the Labour Ministry's mining safety bureau, as saying.

China desperately needed to train an army of professional mining safety supervisors, Liu said. China had just 2,000 mining safety inspectors to keep tabs on 120,000 privately-run mines, 110,000 collective mining companies and 8,000 state-owned mining firms.
"The mining industry is generally characterised by poor labour safety conditions and has a history of gas explosions, fires, mudslides and shaft collapses," it said.

About 10,000 people die each year in accidents in China's mines, which include tens of thousands of small-scale mines that operate with little or no safety measures and are staffed by poorly trained workers.
"Accidents involving 10 deaths or more are on the rise, especially in small township or privately run pits," it said.
However, the safety records of state mines had improved in the last few years, the newspaper said. It gave no further details.
